assumptions: Counts are negative binomial with the stated biological coefficient of variation; RNASeqPower's normal approximation to the log-fold-change test.
The depth is the gene's expected count per sample, not the library size.
limits: One gene at a per-gene significance level, by a normal approximation. For a whole experiment at a false discovery rate, or at small n where the approximation does not hold, use plan_rnaseq_experiment (the exact negative-binomial test, and average power across genes).
The biological CV must come from a comparable experiment; it dominates the answer.
bio.jane/contract.question: How many biological replicates, or how much sequencing depth, does an RNA-seq comparison need to detect a fold change in one gene?

description: Sample size and power for an RNA-seq comparison of two groups, one gene at a time: the biological replicates per group needed to detect a fold change at a given sequencing depth and within-group coefficient of variation, or the power, detectable fold change, CV or α a fixed design gives. Leave one of n, cv, effect, alpha and power out (or name it in `solve_for`). Every quantity takes a list, and the answer is the whole grid, so depth against replicates is one call. RNASeqPower 1.52.0 (Hart et al. 2013), reproduced: a negative binomial count with Poisson sequencing noise 1/depth plus biological variance CV².

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

alpha.description: α, the two-sided false-positive rate per gene.

cv.description: the biological coefficient of variation within a group: 0.4 or less for most genes in human studies, about 0.1 in inbred animals (Hart et al.).

cv2.description: the CV within group 2, one per `cv`. Advanced.

depth.description: average depth of coverage of the gene: its expected read count per sample. Hart et al. found most genes at 0.1 per million mapped reads, so 4 at 40 million.

effect.description: the fold change to detect; 2 and 0.5 are the same change.

n.description: biological replicates in group 1 (and in group 2, unless `n2` is given).

n2.description: replicates in group 2, one per `n`. Advanced.

power.description: 1 − β, the chance of detecting the change if it is real. No default: the target is yours to choose.

solve_for.description: the quantity to solve. Left unset, it is the one of n, cv, effect, alpha and power that was not given. Values: n (n per group), cv (CV), effect (fold change), alpha (α), power (power).

name: calculate_rnaseq_power

curve.description: the solved quantity along the first quantity given as a list, one line per value of the second

grid.description: every design in the grid: each quantity, and the solved one

rCall.description: the R call that reproduces the grid

value.description: the solved value, when the design is a single cell
